title: The base of a red gate is measured like any gate
description: On a paid measurement (P128.38, two (iii) runs) the drive's inline base measurement (run-test-gate.py --base-of, bounded by BASE_MEASURE_SECONDS = the 120 s foreground bound) was torn down, recorded not-knowable, and the drive then took the no-base path and resumed the writer twice over a red the base reproduces case for case. The base measurement is the one gate the drive still runs inline past the one background rule.
desiredOutcome: A red task gate whose base run outlives the Bash foreground bound is measured in the background and stops as gate-red-base when the base reproduces it, with no writer session resumed; a base that cannot be known stops the drive with its own answer

tasks.title: A red gate's base is measured in the background under the one gate rule, and an unknowable base stops the drive instead of resuming the writer
tasks.description:
plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py measures a red task gate's base inline: base_reading_for -> measure_base -> _base_in runs run-test-gate.py --base-of <runId> --record in a detached tree under run_verb_bounded(..., BASE_MEASURE_SECONDS) (around line 2780-2930). When that run outlives 120 s it is torn down and recorded verdict not-knowable, and gate_red_decision then treats the red as introduced and returns gate-red-writer (resume) - so a red the base reproduces spends writer rounds and the run stops at round 2/2. Observed on P128.38: the failing suite's base run under a sandbox takes longer than 120 s; the one failing case fails at the base, case for case.

REQUIRED, as one rule rather than a special case:
1. The base measurement is a drive gate step like the task gate: it goes through gate_in_background's decision (always a step of its own under auto; unmeasured or past the foreground bound -> background; measured under the bound -> may stay inline), is launched as a dispatch with a self-contained run: command (build the detached tree at the red run's head, run run-test-gate.py --base-of --record with no 120 s cut, tear the tree down through remove_base_tree, record the reading on the start's baseMeasured mark), waited on, and decided from what it recorded - the same launch/wait/read-back shape as launch_gate / background_gate / gate_wait_said. Reuse those helpers or factor a shared one; do not write a second copy of the launch-wait-readback machinery. The kill safety the inline path has (mark before the run naming the tree and pids, sweep_base_trees removing a killed run's tree) must hold for the background run too.
2. A base reading that is not knowable (the base run produced no row, failed, or was really cut) must NOT fall through to gate-red-writer or spend a writer round. It stops as a distinct decision (name it e.g. gate-red-base-unknown) whose options are rerun (measure the gate again), measure-base (measure the base again, clearing the start's mark) and block (with --reason); add it to DECISIONS, the step text table, the decision kind map, --explain and every table the drive's own lints hold decisions to. no-base (no comparable base run and none measurable because HEAD moved) keeps its current meaning unless the same reasoning applies - state the choice in the outcome.
3. drive-phase.py auto (the prompt hook's driver) must run the new step without a model, as it runs dispatch-gate/wait-gate today.
4. Prose that describes the base measurement must say the new behaviour: plugins/audit/reference/execute-task.md (the recorded-gate step, around line 265), plugins/audit/reference/orchestrator.md (around line 16-19), PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (around lines 4907 and 4957), and the comment block above BASE_MEASURE_VERDICTS. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

CASES (tests/test_drive_phase.py; tests/test_drive_without_model.py if auto is touched):
- the k15n shape: a red task gate, a base run that outlives the foreground bound (simulate with a stub run-test-gate whose --base-of sleeps past a shortened bound or reports a long recorded mean - do not sleep 120 s in a suite), the base reproduces every failing case -> the drive dispatches the base measurement to the background, reads it back, and decides gate-red-base; no gate-red-writer, no resume, writer resumes counter unchanged.
- a base that cannot be known -> the new stop decision with options rerun/measure-base/block, and no writer round spent.
- measure-base clears the mark and measures again; a killed background base run leaves a tree that the next drive sweeps.
- under auto the base step runs without a model.
Prove each red-first: mutate the fix (e.g. route not-knowable back to gate-red-writer; restore the inline bounded call), assert the mutation landed, and show the case goes red; restore in the same command. Purge __pycache__ between mutate/restore.

DEPENDANTS (owe a check, each named in the outcome): tests/test_drive_phase.py, tests/test_drive_without_model.py (auto's step table), tests/test_run_test_gate.py and tests/test__evidence_io.py if --base-of or base_run change, tests/test__impact.py (reads drive-phase decision tables), tools/_suite.py, the decision tables gate-parity / lints hold to SECURITY.md and docs, plugins/audit/scripts/governance/run-test-gate.py (--base-of contract).

tasks.title: The background base run and next never lose each other's state, and the gate verdict after a base run is read back, never measured again inline
tasks.description:
The phase review of P161.1 (e4e4e4f6) found these in plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py. Fix the class, not each instance.

MED 1. base-run (the background base measurement) and next both read-modify-write the one drive state file. base-run takes no lock (fresh_keeper, near line 3011). next reads the state once at drive() (near line 10918) and writes its copy back repeatedly: take_lock, sweep_base_trees, drive_locked, give_back_lock. A next during a running base-run is the normal case under wait-base and in waves, and it overwrites base-run's done/reading. cut_short then reads that as unknowable and gives a false gate-red-base-unknown. Or the lost ran=True makes base_waiting loop and start a second base run. Required: base-run writes its progress and result only to a file of its own per launch under the drive's state dir (keyed by task and launch), written atomically. next folds that file into the mark when it reads. No process but next writes the shared state file. Remove the comment that accepts the lost write.

MED 2. write_state (near line 1309) opens the file with "w" and dumps into it, which is not atomic. Make every state write atomic: a temp file in the same directory, then os.replace. Move started(proc.pid) (near line 1189) inside run_verb_bounded's try, so a raising callback still tears the group down. The started callback must report a state failure, not raise.

MED 3. base_gate (near line 3143) gets the red verdict back after a base run by calling task_gate/record_gate directly. When the red row cannot be repeated (a timed-out row, a rerun mark that adds --no-reuse, a changed tree), the whole slow gate runs inline and unbounded inside next, which is the shape this phase removes. Record the red run's id and status on the base mark at launch, and read the verdict back through read_back (unrepeatable_red for a row no repeat may copy), the same path background_gate uses.

LOW, same change:
(a) A mark the previous version wrote for a cut base ({verdict: not-knowable, run: None}, with no ran/background key) must read as unknowable, not fall to gate-red-writer.
(b) Apply a mark's reading only to the red run it was measured for (held['of'] equals the row's run or the run it repeats). Otherwise it is unknowable.
(c) gate-red-base-unknown's rule text names the owner's commit-task-work.py --override-verdict route, as gate-red-base does, and offers resume and retry as answers that are never recommended. A base that can never be measured must not be a dead end for a real regression. Nothing is sent without an explicit answer.

Cases for each, red-first: mutate the fix, assert the mutation landed, see the case go red, and restore in the same command. Purge __pycache__ between cycles. Simulate interleaving deterministically, by calling base-run's writer and next's read/write in a chosen order, not with sleeps. Dependants: tests/test_drive_without_model.py (auto runs base-run), tests/test__worktrees.py, and the prose in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md and execute-task.md that describes the base run and the unknown stop. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: A red in a derived gate step has its base measured through the failing suites it names, and a step that cannot be re-run is no-base, not an unknown stop
tasks.description:
A red in a step the gate derives (affected/related, affected/python and the like) cannot have its base measured: run-test-gate.py --base-of runs only the red steps whose command the row keeps verbatim (base_commands, near line 5209), and a derived step's row keeps digests only. So --base-of exits 2 "nothing to run at its base". Since P161.1 the drive reads that as an unknowable base and stops as gate-red-base-unknown. Before that it sent the red to the writer as no-base. Either way the question "does the base fail the same cases" goes unanswered for every derived step, which is where most task-gate reds land. It is the same class as a cut base run.

REQUIRED, one rule:
1. --base-of measures a derived red step at the base by running the failing suites that step's row names (its failing cases are per suite path), with the command the runner derives for those suites the way the gate itself derives it. Reuse the derivation run-test-gate uses for affected steps (_affected, _suite_at_base, base_red); do not write a second spelling of the runner command. The base row then reads like any other base run, and base_red compares case by case.
2. Where a derived step's base genuinely cannot be re-run (no failing suite named, a runner with no per-suite command), --base-of says so per step in its JSON answer (notRun with the reason). The drive then treats that step's base as no-base, structurally unmeasurable like a moved HEAD: the red goes to the writer as it did before P161. It is not the unknown stop, which stays for a base run that was started and was cut, killed, or left no row. State the choice in the code comment above the decision.
3. Cases (tests/test_run_test_gate.py, tests/test_drive_phase.py): a red affected step whose failing suite fails the same case at base gives gate-red-base with no writer round; a red affected step whose suite is green at base goes to the writer; a derived step that cannot be re-run gives no-base and goes to the writer, not gate-red-base-unknown. Red-first for each: mutate the fix, assert the mutation landed, and restore in the same command. Purge __pycache__.

Dependants: tests/test__evidence_io.py, tests/test__affected.py (if present), tests/test_drive_without_model.py, and the prose in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md and plugins/audit/reference/execute-task.md that describes --base-of and the unknown stop. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

outcome.technical: run-test-gate.py: base_commands(row, manifest, phase_id, tree) now returns (commands, published, left). A red step whose row keeps its command verbatim runs as recorded (and stays published). A red DERIVED step goes through the new _derived_at_base: its arm is read off the name, its suites are _ev.named_failing_suites([step]) (the suites its failing cases are recorded under), and the command comes from _affected.entries_for([{path, arm}], phase, meta, tree), the same derivation affected_steps/steps_for use, so the runner command is not spelled a second time. Derived commands stay unpublished, so the row keeps a digest as the task run did; _record_base_run now takes the published list. A step that cannot be re-run goes into left as {name, reason}. Reasons: arm not in _affected.ARMS, runner named no failing suite, entries_for's widen reason (no path-scoped spelling), no command spelled, declared step kept as a digest. _run_base_of passes row.phaseId or args.phase. When nothing can run, --json now prints the answer shape (steps [], notRun with reasons, baseRed null, runId null) and exits E_ASK as before; the text form names each step with its reason. notRun is now a list of {name, reason} instead of a list of names. git grep found no other reader of notRun or base_commands. drive-phase.py: new base_unrunnable(answer) returns the joined reasons only when the answer ran nothing (steps == []) and every red step is in notRun. _base_in returns a fourth value, measurable, which is False only on that answer. measure_base passes it through, so take_base marks measurable False and unknowable False, the row's no-base reading stands, and base_reading_for sends the red to the writer (gate-red-writer) and not to gate-red-base-unknown. That stop is kept for a base run that was cut, killed, failed or left no reading. The choice is stated in the section comment ("A BASE NO COMMAND CAN RUN IS NOT A BASE NOBODY KNOWS") and in a comment above the decision in _base_in. Docs: run-test-gate.py's --base-of section comment, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (the run-test-gate --base-of paragraph and the drive-phase unknown-stop paragraph) and execute-task.md step 3 now describe a derived step's base being measured, notRun, and an unrunnable base going to the writer. M2 (base_unrunnable always None) turned bdr3 red with gate-red-base-unknown. M2b, the over-fire direction (any notRun read as unrunnable), turned bdr1 and bdr2 red. M3 (no JSON when nothing runs) turned bod3 red. Before the fix, bod1-bod3 failed by assertion with exit 2 'digests only', bod4 raised TypeError on the old signature, and bdr1-bdr3 were red. Sweeps: the three named suites exit 0 ('3/3 files ok, 1645 cases'). The lint and dependant suites test__deps, test__output_lints, test__refs, test__evidence_io and test__affected_tests exit 0 ('5/5 files ok, 1144 cases'). house_style_violations returned [], prose_number_claims and doc_prose_numbers report nothing in the changed files, and measure-context --gate exits 0 (GATE OK). tasks.title: An unknown base is the owner's to answer, a base that could not be re-run never decides a later red, and one launch has one base run
tasks.description:
The second phase review of P161 (63a1fb5b, 25d80df7) found these. Fix them in one change.

MED 1. plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py SIGNAL_VERBS (near line 901): decide-gate-red-base-unknown is a judge decision, and orchestrator.md lets the orchestrator answer a judge by itself. The decision now offers resume (a writer round) and retry (an attempt), so an orchestrator can spend a writer round on a red nothing blames on the task, which this phase exists to prevent. "Never recommended" lives only in the rule text. Required: signal it as ask, the way decide-gate-red-base is, so the owner answers it. Update every table the drive's lints hold signal kinds to, and the prose naming it. A case: the unknown stop signals ask.

MED 2. base_reading_for (near lines 3301-3315) with base_measure_due (near line 2880). After a first red whose base could not be re-run (the mark holds measurable False, reading None, of = the first run), a writer round's next red has a new run id. base_measure_due is False because the mark exists, mine is False, and the not-mine branch stops as gate-red-base-unknown. So every later round of an unrunnable derived red, and of the HEAD-moved case, stops for the owner. Required: a mark with measurable False never decides a different red. Treat it as no mark for a red it was not taken for, so that red is measured again (and may now be runnable), or goes to the writer as no-base when it still cannot be run. A case: two unrunnable reds in one start, where the second gives gate-red-writer.

LOW 3. run-test-gate.py _derived_at_base (near lines 5228-5236) spells the base command from the runner's failingSuites paths. The derivation at HEAD spelled it from the paths in the step's name. Map each named suite to the name-listed path it matches with _ev.listed_by(suite, _ev.derived_step_suites(name)) and spell that path. When none matches, put the step in notRun with that reason. A case: the runner prints a path relative to its own directory while the step name spells it from the repository root.

LOW 4. base_run (near lines 3374-3391): two base-run processes for one launch both pass the ran check before either writes. Claim the launch's record first with an exclusive create (O_CREAT|O_EXCL on the record or a .claim beside it). A second process exits with a usage error naming the running one. A case: a second base-run for a claimed launch refuses and measures nothing.

Red-first for each new case: mutate the fix, assert the mutation landed, see the case go red, and restore in the same command. Purge __pycache__ between cycles. Dependants: tests/test_drive_without_model.py (auto and the ask signal), plugins/audit/reference/orchestrator.md and execute-task.md, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.
